recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a targeted active-source fix that aligns stale definition text with the Jira resolution and existing CarePlan element target profiles; no separate related issue needs follow-up from this reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-5756 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care ballot issue asking to broaden the CarePlan definition for shared decision-making and to make clear that patients and RelatedPersons can author and participate in CarePlans.
initial_application: The 2015 CarePlan rework commit db4ace37c6615c9732f958d34d6286fe739fc657 explicitly listed #5756 and added Patient/RelatedPerson support to old CarePlan author, participant, and performer structures. A 2015 follow-up introduction commit added self-maintained patient or care-giver authored examples, and later refactors preserved Patient and RelatedPerson targets on current CarePlan custodian, contributor, reported, and performer elements. The resource-level definition and the active Nutrition module row still retained practitioner-only wording.
additional_context: CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini, and nutrition-module.html is referenced by source/hierarchy.xml and module lists. A 2021 Zulip implementers discussion confirms the current interpretation that CarePlans do not have to come from clinicians and can be created by patients. No direct Confluence reference or conflicting later community decision was found.
reconciliation: Changed source/careplan/structuredefinition-CarePlan.xml at the top-level description and CarePlan root definition to say care may be intended by practitioners, the patient, related persons, or other participants. Changed source/nutrition-module.html to align the active Nutrition module CarePlan summary with the same broadened semantics.
source_changes: source/careplan/structuredefinition-CarePlan.xml: broadened the CarePlan StructureDefinition description and root definition from practitioner-only wording to patient/RelatedPerson-inclusive intended-care wording.
source/nutrition-module.html: aligned the active Nutrition module CarePlan row with the broadened CarePlan definition.
